author: human
request:
Bug report: opening /owners?page=0 — or any page value below 1 — renders the
error page instead of the owner list. Expected behavior: the owner listing
treats any page value below 1 as the first page and responds with the normal
listing (HTTP 200). Find the cause, fix it, and cover the fix with a test.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Owner listing treats a page number below one as the first page
summary: Opening the owner listing with a page number of zero or below renders the error page. The listing must instead treat any page number below one as the first page and respond with the normal listing.
acceptance_criteria: given a request for the owner listing with page 0, when it runs, then the response succeeds (HTTP 200) with the normal owner list view, not the error page
given a request for the owner listing with a negative page number (e.g. -1), when it runs, then the response succeeds (HTTP 200) with the normal owner list view, not the error page
given a page number below one, when the listing is shown, then it holds the same owners and reports the same current page as a request for page 1
non_goals: Changing behavior for page numbers above the last page, or for non-numeric page values: the intake names only page values below 1; both stay open and unchanged by this slice
notes: Grounded in intake-decision line 1 (no recorded decisions; request text only). The request is a defect fix that adds a boundary rule under the owner listing of REQ-OWN-002; it conflicts with no requirement or Non-Goals row. REQ-SYS-002 still governs genuine failures. test_names is one data-driven test covering page 0 and a negative page. PRD updated: docs/prd.md Owner records narrative and Done-when bullet for REQ-OWN-005. No prd-autofix records to audit.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Covered by architecture-principles.md § Tactical Patterns, Web controller row: normalizing a request parameter to its permitted range is binding, not a business rule, so the clamp belongs in OwnerController. system-design.md § Contracts OwnerController row (search with paging) now also implements REQ-OWN-005; that is the only docs write. Root cause (grep basis, IDE oracle not connected): OwnerController.processFindForm binds page with default 1 and findPaginatedForOwnersLastName builds PageRequest.of(page - 1, pageSize); a page below 1 yields a negative index, PageRequest rejects it with IllegalArgumentException, and the error page renders. Clamp page to at least 1 once, at the top of processFindForm, before both the query and addPaginationModel, so the currentPage model attribute reports 1 (acceptance criterion 3). No new type, module, or pattern.
integration_points: Framework transport: MockMvc drives the real MVC dispatch and binding (CLAUDE.md Testing Strategy, the one sanctioned mock); the test sits at the web level per testing-principles.md, which assigns controller normalization to web-level tests

Repository boundary: follow the existing OwnerControllerTests setup for OwnerRepository (the established double in that suite); assert the model's currentPage equals 1 and the listing matches a page-1 request, without adding new stubs beyond what the page-1 path already uses
Binding: no new entry point; page stays a request-scoped int @RequestParam on the existing handler

risks.risk: Clamping only inside findPaginatedForOwnersLastName would leave currentPage reporting 0 or negative in the model, failing acceptance criterion 3
risks.mitigation: Normalize once at the handler entry and pass the clamped value to both the query and addPaginationModel (architecture-principles.md Web controller row)

risks.risk: Owner listing path scales with owner count; system-design.md has no Scale and Load section to cite
risks.mitigation: Path already paged at fixed size via OwnerRepository; slice changes only the page index. Simplest readable form

notes: No design-doc-autofix records to audit. Out of scope per prd-entry non_goals: pages above the last page and non-numeric values stay unchanged. VetController's pagination helper likely shares the same page - 1 construction; it is not part of this slice and the implementer must not touch it. The system-design.md Scale and Load section is absent, a brief gap for a later dispatch; this slice adds no data-scaling path.

author: change-grader
summary: clamp owner listing page below 1 to page 1

blast_radius.note: One production edit in OwnerController.processFindForm (three lines), one added parameterized test, and two one-line doc updates (PRD requirement and the system-design row); nothing under a sensitive path, one module.

semantic_surprise.note: The diff adds Math.max(requestedPage, 1) before every use of page. Both PageRequest.of(page - 1, 5) at line 136 and the currentPage model attribute read the clamped value, the wire name stays 'page' through @RequestParam(name = "page"), and valid pages (>= 1) pass through unchanged. Non-numeric input still fails binding as before, which falls outside this requirement.

test_adequacy.note: The parameterized test covers 0 and -1 and asserts status 200, the ownersList view, and currentPage == 1. Without the clamp, PageRequest.of(-1 or -2) throws, so the test would fail against the old code. The repository stub matches any Pageable, so the offset sent to the query goes unasserted, but the currentPage assertion and the exception path make up for that.

reviewer_hedging.note: All four roster reviewers approved with no findings. The security reviewer cites PageRequest.of at OwnerController.java:131, but that call is at line 136, so one citation does not resolve (the claim itself holds on reading). The test reviewer's recommendation to add a shared anOwner() factory is test-data polish; its grep citations (lines 76, 148, 156, 190, 277) check out.

scope_deviation.note: Zero build retries, consultations, and design revisions. The code does exactly what the single Done-when bullet asks (page zero or below shows the first page), and the doc edits only register REQ-OWN-005 in the PRD and on the OwnerController row.

rationale: The change is small, in scope, and correct on reading: the clamp feeds both the repository offset and currentPage, and a real boundary test covers it. The only flag is a mis-cited line in the security approval. Glance at OwnerController.java:95-97 and the new test, then merge.
